For locally advanced gastrointestinal stromal tumors (GISTs), neoadjuvant imatinib treatment may be considered as part of the management strategy. Imatinib is a tyrosine kinase inhibitor that targets the KIT and PDGFRA genes, which are commonly mutated in GISTs.

Regarding kit mutation analysis, it can indeed provide valuable information for determining the appropriate treatment approach. Upfront evaluation of kit mutation status may help in identifying potentially biologically different tumors and assessing the correct timing of surgery. This is because some GISTs with specific mutations may require earlier or later surgical intervention.

In summary, kit mutation analysis can be a useful tool in guiding neoadjuvant imatinib treatment in locally advanced GISTs by helping to identify which patients are most likely to benefit from this therapeutic approach and when it would be appropriate to proceed with surgery.
